const answer = `IDEA: holonomy-frame-sid
TITLE: Behavioural-drift holonomy rotates the per-prefix code frame of the hyperbolic RQ-VAE, so a prefix's successor displacement (not its radius) decides which codewords its items receive.
MOTIVATION: Round one showed the flat parts of the problem: level 1 already uses ~all 256 codewords, while levels 2 and 3 collapse to 1769 and 2201 distinct prefixes over 24556 items (~11 items per deepest triple). The ranking cannot move unless the PREFIX STRUCTURE moves, i.e. unless items that share an (L1,L2,L3) triple stop sharing it. At the same time issue 126 says the radial coordinate is only group compactness and that permuting radii destroys the correlation, while Gromov-delta and ancestor-depth weighting actively hurt. So the useful behaviour signal is a CONTRAST/direction signal, and the useful geometric object is not a radius but a frame. This idea turns the single most geometry-specific quantity that has no Euclidean analogue - the holonomy (the rotation a tangent vector picks up when parallel-transported around a closed geodesic loop) - into the thing that orients the residual codebook of every prefix, driven by where that prefix's training-only successors actually go.
NOVELTY: Not a weighted assignment, not a Frechet codebook update, not a per-level curvature, not an entropy-ranked radius, not Gromov-delta weighting. The curvature is FIXED at c=1 (gauge-fixed, exactly as issue 126(b) requires) and no curvature is learned; what is learned/measured is the AREA of a geodesic triangle (origin, prefix text anchor, prefix successor anchor), and that area is used as a holonomy rotation of the code frame in the 2-plane spanned by the two anchors' disagreement. The mechanism is provably inert (identical to the baseline assignment) when behaviour adds no directional information, and it is also inert in the Euclidean limit, so it cannot be a behaviour suffix on an unchanged quantizer. Nothing in the earlier rounds used holonomy or a frame rotation.
CHANGE: For every prefix p we build a successor anchor b_p by propagating the frozen text embeddings through the row-normalised training transition matrix, and a text anchor a_p from the prefix's own items; the hyperbolic area of (origin, a_p, b_p) sets an angle theta_p, and each level's shared 256-codeword codebook is rotated by theta_p about a_p before nearest-neighbour assignment inside p. Prefixes whose items lead where they already are get theta_p = 0 and keep their baseline codes; prefixes whose successors drift away get a distinct, area-determined frame, which de-aliases the deep triples.
SPECIFICATION:
Notation: z_i in R^32 is the frozen Stage-1 text embedding (identical to the baseline, no trainable encoder - this is the variant of round one that did not collapse). Ball map psi(z) = tanh(||z||/s) * z/||z|| with s = mean ||z|| over the 24556 items (a derived, scale-relative constant), c = 1, ball radius 1.
(1) Behaviour matrix from the Stage-2 training split only: T[a,b] = number of consecutive pairs a->b in the training histories. P(b|a) = T[a,b] / sum_b T[a,b] (rows with zero mass dropped).
(2) For prefix p with item set S_p: a_p = psi(mean_{i in S_p} z_i); v_p(b) = (1/|S_p|) * sum_{i in S_p} P(b|i); b_p = psi(sum_b v_p(b) z_b). Note b_p lives in the SAME frozen text ball, so no cross-space projection is needed; behaviour enters only through v_p.
(3) Poincare distance d(u,v) = arcosh(1 + 2||u-v||^2 / ((1-||u||^2)(1-||v||^2))). Sides: A = d(o,b_p) (opposite the angle at a_p), B = d(o,a_p), C = d(a_p,b_p).
(4) Angles by the hyperbolic law of cosines: cos(alpha) = (cosh B cosh C - cosh A)/(sinh B sinh C), and cyclically. Area Delta_p = max(0, pi - (alpha+beta+gamma)). Holonomy theta_p = wrap_to_(-pi,pi](-Delta_p) (Gauss-Bonnet, K = -1).
(5) Frame at a_p: e1 = log_{a_p}(b_p)/||log_{a_p}(b_p)|| (if ||log|| < 1e-8 then theta_p := 0); u_text = top principal direction of {log_{a_p}(z_i) : i in S_p}; e2 = orthonormalise(u_text - <u_text,e1> e1). Let R_p = identity except on span(e1,e2), where it is the 2x2 rotation by theta_p.
(6) Rotated codebook for prefix p at level l: c'_{p,k} = exp_{a_p}( R_p log_{a_p}(c^l_k) ), k = 1..256. Assignment k_i = argmin_k d(z_i^l, c'_{p(i),k})^2 (ties broken by smallest k); residual z_i^{l+1} = log_{c'_{p,k_i}}(z_i^l) as in the baseline RQ. Level 1 uses p = root (a_p = origin) so its frame is untouched and all 256 codewords stay in play.
(7) Stage 2 then trains exactly the frozen recipe on the reconstruction of the frozen text geometry; only the decoder/residual parameters move, the frames are computed once at epoch 0 and re-checked every 100 epochs for prefix-set drift.
Pseudocode: build T; psi all z; for l in 1..3: for each active prefix p: compute a_p, v_p, b_p, Delta_p, theta_p, R_p; build c'_{p,.}; assign all items in p; update prefix sets. Then run RQ-VAE training with these fixed per-prefix codebooks.
COST: One static pass per epoch-0 plus a refresh every 100 epochs: for 256 active prefixes per level x 3 levels, each pass is about 3 x 256 x (32-d log/exp + a 32x32 rotation) = O(1e6) flops, i.e. milliseconds. Per step the extra work is rotating the codebook of each prefix present in the 4096-item batch (at most 32 prefixes x 256 codes x 32 dims = 2.6e5 flops) plus one Poincare distance matrix instead of a Euclidean one (4096 x 256 x 32 = 3.4e7 flops); measured expectation +5 to +10% on the 0.145 s/epoch baseline, i.e. ~0.152-0.160 s/epoch and 585-605 s for the 3000-epoch, 24-step, 4-GPU run. Stage 3 is untouched (frozen protocol, 150 epochs).
HYPOTHESIS: If the deep-prefix aliasing is the binding capacity problem and if behaviour adds directional information beyond text only where the prefix's successors drift, then rotating only the drifting prefixes' frames should raise the number of distinct L3 triples above 2201 and lower the items-per-triple tail, and raise Stage 3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 by giving the generator finer distinctions among the most frequently queried items. Observable: distinct L3 triples, the 95th percentile of items-per-triple, per-prefix conditional entropy of the L3 code, and finally test_recall@10 / recall@5 / ndcg@10 on the frozen 57439-query protocol.
RISKS: (a) A rigid rotation per prefix can act like a relabelling: if the level-3 codebook is close to rotationally symmetric the partition barely changes, and the triples change without gaining information. (b) If successor drift is dominated by global popularity, v_p is nearly the same for every prefix, all theta_p cluster near one value, and the mechanism degrades to a single global relabelling. (c) Large areas produce large rotations that scatter codes arbitrarily and can hurt, especially for the 5 prefixes that survive one codeword over. (d) The 100-epoch refresh makes the frames piecewise constant, so late-training prefix drift is only partially tracked. (e) Single run, so seed noise of +/-0.003 on recall cannot be separated from a real gain.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Prefix-conditioned successor displacement: the training-only distribution over next items given each item, aggregated over the items of a prefix, and compared with the prefix's own text position.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: Directed consecutive-pair counts T[a,b] from Stage-2 training user histories only, row-normalised to P(b|a); prefix successor weight v_p(b) = mean over i in S_p of P(b|i); b_p = psi(sum_b v_p(b) z_b). No validation or test interaction is ever read, and T is built once before training starts.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: T, v_p, a_p and b_p use only Stage-2 training histories and the frozen Stage-1 text embeddings; the prefix sets S_p are produced by the model's own training-time assignment. Validation and test sequences are never touched: the frames are a deterministic function of (training transitions, frozen text vectors), so an item's SID cannot depend on any held-out interaction, and there is no path by which a test query can alter theta_p or c'_{p,k}.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Poincare ball with FIXED curvature c = 1 (gauge-fixed; no learned curvature), using the Poincare distance, the log/exp maps at a_p, and the geodesic-triangle area via Gauss-Bonnet, whose holonomy is -Area. The rotation R_p itself is a hyperbolic isometry about a_p.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Inside quantization, at every RQ level, immediately before the nearest-codeword assignment and inside the decode of the assigned code: the shared codebook of a prefix is expressed in the prefix's own holonomy-rotated frame.
COUPLING PATH: transition counts -> successor anchor b_p -> hyperbolic triangle (origin, a_p, b_p) -> area -> holonomy angle theta_p -> rotation R_p of the level-l codebook -> assignment k_i -> SID token -> Stage 3. Removing behaviour sets b_p := a_p, the triangle degenerates, Delta_p = 0, theta_p = 0 and every prefix keeps the baseline codes; removing geometry sets Delta_p := 0 (the Euclidean holonomy is trivial) and the assignment becomes the Euclidean baseline. Neither term survives alone.
COUPLING EQUATION: c'_{p,k} = exp^{c=1}_{a_p}( R_{e1,e2}(theta_p) log^{c=1}_{a_p}(c_k) ), with theta_p = -Area_c( o, a_p(w_behaviour), b_p(w_behaviour) ) and b_p = psi(sum_b v_p(b) z_b), v_p(b) proportional to sum_{i in S_p} P_train(b|i).
OBSERVABLES: distinct L3 prefixes (baseline 2201), distinct L2 prefixes (baseline 1769), the items-per-triple distribution and its 95th percentile, per-prefix conditional entropy of the L3 code, the fraction of prefixes with |theta_p| > 1e-3, the per-epoch reconstruction loss, SID coverage, and Stage 3 test_recall@10 (target > 0.065, baseline 0.0679, round-one 0.05439), recall@5 and ndcg@10.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: use_behaviour_anchor = False: set v_p(b) := uniform over S_p (or equivalently b_p := a_p), so Delta_p = 0, theta_p = 0, all R_p = I and the assignment is exactly the baseline; wired in code, not trained.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: use_hyperbolic = False: set theta_p := 0 and use the Euclidean distance and Euclidean exp/log, so the holonomy channel is provably zero and the quantizer reduces to the Euclidean RQ-VAE; wired in code, not trained.
ABLATION BOTH ON: the full run described above, the only arm actually trained: 3000 Stage-2 epochs on four GPUs at global batch 4096, then the frozen 150-epoch Stage 3.
SPEC EQUATIONS: see steps (1)-(7): d(u,v) = arcosh(1 + 2||u-v||^2/((1-||u||^2)(1-||v||^2))); log_a(b), exp_a(v) = tanh(||v||) (v/||v||) under the standard ball formulas; cos(alpha) = (cosh B cosh C - cosh A)/(sinh B sinh C); Delta = pi - (alpha+beta+gamma); theta = -Delta; c'_{p,k} = exp_{a_p}(R_p log_{a_p}(c_k)); k_i = argmin_k d(z_i^l, c'_{p(i),k})^2.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: frozen text embeddings z_i in R^32 for 24556 items, training transition counts T, the 3 x 256 codebook of the baseline RQ-VAE, and the current prefix assignment. Outputs: for each active prefix and level a 256 x 32 rotated codebook c'_{p,.}, a per-prefix angle table theta (256 x 3), and the resulting SID matrix (24556 x 3) plus the prefix sets used by the next level.
SAFEGUARDS: map every vector with psi and clip the ball norm to 1 - 1e-3; clamp every cosh argument to [0, 30] and every cos(alpha) to [-1+1e-7, 1-1e-7] before arccos; clip Delta_p to [0, pi] and set theta_p := 0 whenever any side length is below 1e-8, any value is non-finite, or |theta_p| < 1e-6 (degenerate triangle); wrap theta to (-pi, pi]; orthonormalise (e1,e2) by Gram-Schmidt and fall back to theta_p = 0 if ||e2|| < 1e-6; verify R_p is orthogonal to 1e-5; assert the angle table is finite and log the fraction of prefixes with nonzero theta; make the assignment deterministic by breaking ties on the smallest code index; the rotation is an isometry about a_p, so it cannot shrink the codebook toward the origin and cannot reproduce the round-one zero-residual collapse, and since the text geometry is frozen the collapse mode of a trainable encoder feeding the curved chain is not reachable.
END IDEA`;

HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Inside quantization, at every RQ level, immediately before the nearest-codeword assignment and inside the decode of the assigned code: the shared codebook of a prefix is expressed in that prefix's own holonomy-rotated frame.
COUPLING PATH: transition counts -> successor anchor b_p -> hyperbolic triangle (origin, a_p, b_p) -> area -> holonomy angle theta_p -> rotation R_p of the level-l codebook -> assignment k_i -> SID token -> Stage 3. Removing behaviour sets b_p := a_p, the triangle degenerates, Delta_p = 0, theta_p = 0 and every prefix keeps the baseline codes; removing geometry sets Delta_p := 0 (Euclidean holonomy is trivial) and the assignment becomes the Euclidean baseline. Neither term survives alone.
COUPLING EQUATION: c'_{p,k} = exp^{c=1}_{a_p}( R_{e1,e2}(theta_p) log^{c=1}_{a_p}(c_k) ), with theta_p = -Area_c( o, a_p(w_behaviour), b_p(w_behaviour) ) and b_p = psi(sum_b v_p(b) z_b), v_p(b) proportional to sum_{i in S_p} P_train(b|i).
OBSERVABLES: distinct L3 prefixes (baseline 2,201), distinct L2 prefixes (baseline 1,769), the items-per-triple distribution and its 95th percentile, per-prefix conditional entropy of the L3 code, the fraction of prefixes with |theta_p| > 1e-3, per-epoch reconstruction loss, SID coverage (all 24,556 items, 251 L1 codewords), and Stage 3 test_recall@10 (target > 0.065; baseline 0.0679; round-one 0.05439), recall@5 and ndcg@10.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: use_behaviour_anchor = False: set v_p(b) uniform over S_p (equivalently b_p := a_p), so Delta_p = 0, theta_p = 0, all R_p = I and the assignment is exactly the baseline; wired in code, never trained.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: use_hyperbolic = False: set theta_p := 0 and use the Euclidean distance and Euclidean exp/log, so the holonomy channel is provably zero and the quantizer reduces to the Euclidean RQ-VAE; wired in code, never trained.
ABLATION BOTH ON: the full run above, the only arm actually trained: 3000 Stage-2 epochs on four GPUs at global batch 4096, then the frozen 150-epoch Stage 3.
SPEC EQUATIONS: see steps (1)-(7); d(u,v) = arcosh(1 + 2||u-v||^2/((1-||u||^2)(1-||v||^2))); exp_a(v) = tanh(||v||)(v/||v||), log_a its inverse, both in the c = 1 ball; cos(alpha) = (cosh B cosh C - cosh A)/(sinh B sinh C); Delta = pi - (alpha+beta+gamma); theta = -Delta; c'_{p,k} = exp_{a_p}(R_p log_{a_p}(c_k)); k_i = argmin_k d(z_i^l, c'_{p(i),k})^2.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: frozen text embeddings z_i in R^32 for 24,556 items, training transition counts T, the baseline 3 x 256 codebook, and the current prefix assignment. Outputs: for each active prefix and level a 256 x 32 rotated codebook c'_{p,.}, a per-prefix angle table theta (256 x 3), the SID matrix (24,556 x 3), and the prefix sets consumed by the next level.
SAFEGUARDS: map every vector with psi and clip ball norms to 1 - 1e-3; clamp every cosh argument to [0, 30] and every cos(alpha) to [-1 + 1e-7, 1 - 1e-7] before arccos; clip Delta_p to [0, pi] and set theta_p := 0 whenever any side is below 1e-8, any value is non-finite, or |theta_p| < 1e-6; wrap theta to (-pi, pi]; orthonormalise (e1,e2) by Gram-Schmidt and fall back to theta_p = 0 if ||e2|| < 1e-6; verify R_p orthogonality to 1e-5; assert the angle table is finite and log the fraction of prefixes with nonzero theta; break assignment ties on the smallest code index. Because the rotation is an isometry about a_p it cannot shrink the codebook toward the origin and cannot reproduce the round-one zero-residual collapse, and because the text geometry is frozen the trainable-encoder collapse path is unreachable.
